description: Fine-tune downstream layers (6-11) to accept fixed orthogonal rotation at waist layer 5. Pre-registered thresholds: >70% recovery = alignment sensitivity, <30% = genuine computation destruction.

controls.description: Fine-tuning downstream layers WITHOUT rotation (same number of steps). Control ΔL_target should remain high, confirming that the ΔL reduction is specific to the rotation, not generic drift.

interpretation: 90% recovery far exceeds the pre-registered 70% threshold. Downstream layers can almost fully compensate for the orthogonal rotation in 500 steps, confirming that scrambling damage is primarily about learned basis alignment rather than genuine computation destruction. The ~10% residual may reflect genuinely direction-sensitive computation. Controls confirm this is rotation-specific: fine-tuning without rotation does not reduce ΔL_target.
verdict: CONFIRMED: scrambling measures alignment sensitivity, not functional necessity
